title: Separatedness descends to a stage for a finitely presented algebraic space
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Give spaces the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For morphisms of spaces, separated means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]; a space is quasi-compact if it has a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; a morphism $a:A\to B$ is quasi-compact if $A\times_BC$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C\to B$; quasi-separated means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. A space is quasi-separated if its structure map to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-separated. Locally of finite type and locally of finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and locally of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, where universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (agreeing with the scheme convention [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps, and $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ from an algebraic space. Set $f_i:X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i\to T_i$ for $i\ge i_0$, and $f:X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T\to T$. If $f$ is separated, there is an $i\ge i_0$ such that $f_j$ is separated for every $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 0851 (lemma-descend-separated-morphism), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to a finitely presented space over an affine base; persistence by spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated).

proof.text: Put $T_0=T_{i_0}$, $X_0=X_{i_0}$, $D_0=X_0\times_{T_0}X_0$, and $\delta_0=\Delta_{f_{i_0}}:X_0\to D_0$. The affine scheme $T_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. These are scheme properties; read as properties of the algebraic space $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ they hold as follows. The identity is a representable surjective etale map from the quasi-compact scheme $T_0$, so the space $T_0$ is quasi-compact. Its diagonal $T_0\to T_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}T_0$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the surjective multiplication $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\to A$, hence a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $C\to T_0\times T_0$ is a map from a quasi-compact space with quasi-compact scheme atlas $U\to C$, then $U\times_{T_0\times T_0}T_0\to U$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so its source is a quasi-compact scheme (a closed subset of a quasi-compact space), and it is a surjective etale atlas of $C\times_{T_0\times T_0}T_0$ by the base-change clause of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Hence the structure map of $T_0$ is quasi-separated, i.e. $T_0$ is a quasi-separated space. Finite presentation gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f_{i_0}$. The definition of quasi-compact morphism, applied to $T_0\to T_0$, gives quasi-compactness of $X_0$; the source clause of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] gives quasi-separatedness of $X_0$. Its fibre-product clause gives that $D_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Finally [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-locally-finite-type] says that $\delta_0$ is representable and locally of finite type. Thus both the source and target, not merely the relative morphism, satisfy the hypotheses for closed-immersion descent.

source.place: Tag 0851 (lemma-descend-separated-morphism), the omitted qcqs and local finite type checks; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 04ZH, 073B and 03HK.

proof.text: For every $T_0$-space $B$, transitivity of the sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives $(X_0\times_{T_0}X_0)\times_{T_0}B\cong (X_0\times_{T_0}B)\times_B(X_0\times_{T_0}B)$. On sections over a test scheme this sends $((x_1,x_2),b)$ to $((x_1,b),(x_2,b))$, with inverse forgetting the repeated $b$. The base change of $\delta_0$ sends $(x,b)$ to $((x,x),b)$, so under this identification it is the diagonal of $X_0\times_{T_0}B\to B$. In particular, the limit base change of $\delta_0$ is $\Delta_f$, which is a closed immersion by the separatedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), diagonal base-change formula, written out on sheaf sections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-descend-closed-immersion] to the $T_0$-morphism $\delta_0:X_0\to D_0$ and the given affine base system (restricted to indices at least $i_0$). The source and target are qcqs and $\delta_0$ is locally of finite type by step 1; its limit base change is a closed immersion by step 2. We obtain $i\ge i_0$ for which $(\delta_0)_{T_i}$ is a closed immersion. Step 2 with $B=T_i$ identifies this morphism with $\Delta_{f_i}$. Hence $f_i$ is separated by its definition.

source.place: Tag 0851 (lemma-descend-separated-morphism), application of Tag 0850 to the stage diagonal.

proof.text: For any $j\ge i$, the transitivity identification $(X_0\times_{T_0}T_i)\times_{T_i}T_j\cong X_0\times_{T_0}T_j$ identifies $f_j$ with the base change of $f_i$ along $T_j\to T_i$. The arbitrary base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] therefore makes $f_j$ separated. The same index $i$ works for every $j\ge i$.
